c01s03.title: A tendency and an occasion
c01s03.caption: A broad tendency can coexist with different states. Neither description alone explains the cause.

c01s03b.title: One person can vary across occasions
c01s03b.caption: This conceptual distribution represents variation in one person’s states, not data from a measured volunteer. A typical level does not erase the range.

c01s04.title: Different demands, different expression
c01s04.caption: The contexts offer different demands and opportunities. Repeated observations are needed to test the proposed pattern.

c01s05.title: Study the pattern at two levels
c01s05.caption: Stable differences and state variability are compatible; a distribution is not a complete causal account.

c02s03.title: Dimensions allow degrees, not boxes
c02s03.caption: The five unscored lines represent broad dimensions, not a real person’s profile or a self-assessment. Instrument definitions and norms matter.

c02s03b.title: Similar total, different components
c02s03b.caption: Narrower facets can differ within a similar broad description. No scores are assigned in this fictional comparison.

c02s04.title: Do not turn a dimension into a diagnosis
c02s04.caption: Trait descriptions do not establish a disorder, moral worth or a universal role preference.

c02s05.title: A framework is not a whole person
c02s05.caption: The Big Five are useful and well studied, but do not replace goals, identity, skills or contextual evidence.

c03s03.title: Consistency answers one question
c03s03.caption: Different reliability estimates address different sources of consistency; none grants unrestricted validity.

c03s03b.title: Build a validity argument
c03s03b.caption: Validity supports a specified interpretation and use. Evidence for one setting may not support another.

c03s04.title: Two sources see different things
c03s04.caption: Disagreement can reveal different observation windows or measurement problems rather than one automatically correct account.

c03s05.title: A percentile needs a reference
c03s05.caption: A percentile is not the percentage of personality a person possesses, and extra decimal places do not remove uncertainty.

c04s03.title: Two kinds of stability question
c04s03.caption: The same group can change in average level while retaining a similar relative ordering.

c04s03b.title: Two developmental study designs
c04s03b.caption: Age-related differences and individual change require different comparisons; neither design is free of limitations.

c04s04.title: A role and a trait can be related
c04s04.caption: Existing tendencies can influence role entry while experiences may also contribute to change. The branches show accounts to investigate.

c04s05.title: Average trends leave individual variation
c04s05.caption: A developmental average is not a timetable everyone must follow or proof that one event caused a change.

c05s03.title: Population variation is not an individual split
c05s03.caption: Heritability does not divide one person’s personality into genetic and environmental percentages.

c05s03b.title: A twin comparison is model-based
c05s03b.caption: Twin designs inform genetic contributions under assumptions. They do not identify a unique personality gene.

c05s04.title: Genes and environments can relate differently
c05s04.caption: Gene–environment correlation and interaction answer distinct questions; neither should be inferred from one anecdote.

c05s05.title: Inherited does not mean unchangeable
c05s05.caption: A genetic contribution to differences does not settle whether a changed environment can help.

c06s03.title: Make the proposed pattern specific
c06s03.caption: The fictional behavioral signature is a hypothesis about a meaningful situation feature, not a fixed label.

c06s03b.title: Capability and consequence differ
c06s03b.caption: Believing one can act differs from believing the action will produce a desired result. Actual skill also needs evidence.

c06s04.title: A pattern can reinforce its own context
c06s04.caption: The sequence illustrates a possible feedback process. Choices are constrained, and every link needs evidence in a real case.

c06s05.title: Different levels can complement each other
c06s05.caption: A broad trait summary and a social-cognitive process explanation answer related but different questions.

c07s03.title: Same action, different possible aims
c07s03.caption: The outward action alone does not reveal the motive. The story supplies fictional reasons to illustrate the distinction.

c07s03b.title: Endorsement and pressure differ
c07s03b.caption: Autonomy concerns endorsement, not working alone. Motives can be mixed and vary over time.

c07s04.title: Clarify before adding demands
c07s04.caption: A support plan should be checked against participation and well-being, not attendance alone.

c07s05.title: An attendance count is not a motive measure
c07s05.caption: Motivational interpretations need relevant evidence. Extra hours cannot establish enjoyment by themselves.

c08s03.title: The self can be studied at several levels
c08s03.caption: A trait score, a self-evaluation and a life narrative provide different kinds of information.

c08s03b.title: A story can select a narrow sample
c08s03b.caption: Adding context and exceptions can qualify a narrative without demanding forced optimism.

c08s04.title: Keep sources and purposes visible
c08s04.caption: No single source provides a complete person. Investigate what disagreements between sources mean.

c08s05.title: Association is not a prescribed story
c08s05.caption: An association involving a narrative theme does not prove that imposing that story causes well-being.

c09s03.title: Matching words may not match meaning
c09s03.caption: Measurement comparability requires more than translation, including how behaviors and response scales are understood.

c09s03b.title: Group averages do not fix an individual
c09s03b.caption: Conceptual overlapping distributions illustrate within-group variation. The curves are not measured cultural data or a claim about a particular population.

c09s04.title: Check the reach of the evidence
c09s04.caption: Coverage and measurement evidence set the scope of a conclusion. Local collaboration can expose gaps.

c09s05.title: A failed comparison can reveal a measure problem
c09s05.caption: A measurement problem does not establish that people lack traits, nor does it support a stereotype about a group.

c10s03.title: Ask what the score adds
c10s03.caption: Incremental validity concerns added predictive information, not just whether a score correlates with an outcome somewhere.

c10s03b.title: Match the decision to relevant evidence
c10s03b.caption: A direct low-stakes work sample can answer a role question more closely than an unsupported broad label.

c10s04.title: Keep descriptions revisable
c10s04.caption: A bounded description leaves room for development and does not become a permanent exclusion.

c10s05.title: An association has practical limits
c10s05.caption: Population associations do not validate an unrelated quiz or guarantee one individual’s outcome.
